title: Globally Honest Confidence Sets for Fusing Trials on Different Outcome Scales with Noisy Calibration
banked_reason: D0.5.G tier=subfield below field floor; paper_score_ceiling=6.5 below 7.4; math and decision panels pass, but the 0.01 full-game rational primal-dual enclosure remains open.
gap_reasons: The numerical work establishes only a 0.0959 separation using one feasible fusion rule and a primary-only dual bound; it does not tightly determine the advertised sharp value of Lglobal, as the full primal-dual enclosure remains open.
the paper merely quantifies over schedules whose error decay is assumed, without exhibiting an admissible schedule or proving that the schedule class is nonempty
the proportional-effect link, four-observation calibration design, and connected fused action class are bespoke
proof_attempt_summary: Discovery derived the Gaussian minimax transfer, finite connected-game characterization, and a directed strict-gain certificate. Three bounded soundness repairs resolved the primary-only comparator, LP duality, and certificate/citation integrity; the final math and decision panels passed with no findings. The field-floor review still rated the package subfield because a tight rational primal-dual enclosure of the full calibrated frontier and a verified admissible error schedule remain open.
tldr: Two independent randomized studies measure a common causal treatment contrast on different outcome scales under a prospectively specified exact proportional-effect link, while a separate fixed experiment of four i.i.d. \(N(\alpha,1)\) observations calibrates the scale ratio. These link and calibration conditions are bespoke maintained assumptions. An explicit potential-outcome model with consistency and randomized treatment identifies \(\theta=E[Y(1)-Y(0)]\) and derives the observed Gaussian product law. The paper identifies the sharp asymptotic minimax expected length of connected confidence intervals that cover every finite-sample parameter but are evaluated near a null effect. An exact subexperiment gives the all-procedure converse, while a uniform total-variation reduction and exact coverage repair give attainment. A separate finite primary-only experiment is explicit: its parameter is \((\theta,b_Y)\in[-2,2]^2\), its actions are arbitrary randomized Borel confidence sets with global coverage, and its local scaled expected-measure minimax value converges to \(L_0\) by a nonconnected truncation and completion argument. A proved convergent sequence of fully specified rational finite games with explicit two-sided errors characterizes the fused Gaussian value. An independently replayed byte-level verifier binds the canonical exact-rational archive to the distinct CSV and NPZ inputs actually consumed by the two directed checkers; the fresh checker enclosures certify \(L_{\mathrm{global}}<6.063684<6.159628<L_0\), so calibrated fusion improves the globally honest primary-only benchmark by more than \(0.0959\). The displayed fusion interval is a witness, not an optimizer; the open task is to execute one sufficiently fine full game and serialize its primal and dual optimizers for an enclosure of width at most \(0.01\).
gap: Published disparate-outcome fusion theory distinguishes known from unknown links through regular efficiency, while published confidence-set optimization treats generic expected measure. Fixed noisy calibration lies between those regimes and creates a nonregular confidence problem for which global coverage and local expected length have not been jointly characterized.
fill: The project derives the causal Gaussian product experiment from an explicit i.i.d. potential-outcome randomization model, proves exact finite-sample-to-Gaussian transfer, supplies fully specified rational primal and dual connected-interval games with explicit two-sided errors, and certifies a strict fusion gain over every randomized primary-only confidence set using canonical versioned witness tables.
